$comment: Hand-authored, reviewed once, regulation-specific and customer-independent. Design rationale in docs/bcbs239-policy-design.md. Four policies rather than one (which over-asks every CDE) or eleven (which duplicates, since the principles overlap). The value is in derived_requirements fields a steward must answer per CDE, each traceable to a paragraph — not in restating the regulation in a description.

regulation.title: Principles for effective risk data aggregation and risk reporting

policy_group.title: BCBS 239
policy_group.description:
Principles for effective risk data aggregation and risk reporting (Basel Committee, January 2013). Groups the policies derived from the bank-facing principles 1–11. Principles 12–14 address supervisors and are out of scope.

Source: bis.org/publ/bcbs239.pdf
policy_group.$comment: PREREQUISITE, not created by the kit. Policy groups have no create API (GET /integration/v1/policy_group is read-only), so this group must exist in the instance. The provider resolves it by title and warns if absent. Note the title is NOT namespace-prefixed: it refers to the customer's own object.

policies.title: Risk Data Architecture and Identification
policies.description:
Principle 2 — Data architecture and IT infrastructure. A bank shall maintain integrated data taxonomies and architecture across the banking group, including single identifiers and unified naming conventions, and shall work toward a single authoritative source for risk data per risk type.

¶33: "A bank should establish integrated data taxonomies and architecture across the banking group, which includes information on the characteristics of the data (metadata), as well as use of single identifiers and/or unified naming conventions for data including legal entities, counterparties, customers and accounts."

¶36(d): "A bank should strive towards a single authoritative source for risk data per each type of risk."

policies.title: Risk Data Accuracy and Reconciliation
policies.description:
Principle 3 — Accuracy and Integrity. Risk data shall be aggregated on a largely automated basis so as to minimise the probability of errors, with controls as robust as those applied to accounting data, reconciliation to source systems, and measured, monitored accuracy with defined escalation.

¶36(a): "Controls surrounding risk data should be as robust as those applicable to accounting data."

¶36(c): "Risk data should be reconciled with bank's sources, including accounting data where appropriate, to ensure that the risk data is accurate."

¶40: "Supervisors expect banks to measure and monitor the accuracy of data and to develop appropriate escalation channels and action plans to be in place to rectify poor data quality."

policies.title: Risk Data Completeness
policies.description:
Principle 4 — Completeness. A bank shall capture and aggregate all material risk data across the banking group, including off-balance-sheet exposures, available by business line, legal entity, asset type, industry, region and other groupings relevant to the risk in question. Completeness shall be measured and monitored, and the impact of any incompleteness assessed.

¶41: "A bank's risk data aggregation capabilities should include all material risk exposures, including those that are off-balance sheet."

¶43: "Supervisors expect banks to produce aggregated risk data that is complete and to measure and monitor the completeness of their risk data. Where risk data is not entirely complete, the impact should not be critical."

policies.title: Risk Data Timeliness
policies.description:
Principle 5 — Timeliness. A bank shall be able to generate aggregate, up-to-date risk data in a timely manner while meeting the accuracy, integrity, completeness and adaptability principles, with speed requirements set per risk type and the capability tested under stress conditions.

¶44: "A bank's risk data aggregation capabilities should ensure that it is able to produce aggregate risk information on a timely basis to meet all reporting requirements."

¶46: names the specific critical risks requiring rapid aggregation, including aggregated credit exposure to a large corporate borrower and counterparty credit risk exposures.

standards.purpose: Establish, for each critical data element, whether it has a single authoritative source and a governed enterprise identifier, as Principle 2 requires. Without an authoritative source and a consistent identifier, the same exposure cannot be linked across systems and group-level aggregation is not possible.
standards.scope: Every critical data element used in risk data aggregation, across all legal entities in the banking group.

derived_requirements.name: Authoritative source
derived_requirements.description: Whether a single authoritative source has been identified for this element, per ¶36(d).

derived_requirements.name: Enterprise identifier
derived_requirements.description: Whether this element uses a governed enterprise-wide identifier and naming convention, per ¶33.

standards.purpose: Establish, for each critical data element, whether it is reconciled to its system of record, whether accuracy is monitored with a defined escalation path, and whether manual or end-user-computing intervention in its production is documented. An unverifiable figure is not a compliant one.
standards.scope: Every critical data element that contributes to a reported risk figure.

derived_requirements.name: Reconciliation to system of record
derived_requirements.description: Whether this element is reconciled to accounting or source systems, per ¶36(c).

derived_requirements.name: Accuracy monitoring and escalation
derived_requirements.description: Whether accuracy is measured and monitored with an escalation path, per ¶40.

derived_requirements.name: Manual and EUC intervention
derived_requirements.description: Whether manual processes or desktop applications contribute to this element, and whether that is documented, per ¶36(b) and ¶39.

fields.name: Manual or EUC intervention in the flow

standards.purpose: Establish, for each critical data element, whether completeness is measured and monitored, what coverage exclusions exist, and whether the materiality of those exclusions has been assessed. Principle 4 permits incompleteness only where its impact is understood and not critical.
standards.scope: Every critical data element used to aggregate material risk exposures, including off-balance-sheet positions.

derived_requirements.name: Completeness monitoring
derived_requirements.description: Whether completeness is measured and monitored, per ¶43.

derived_requirements.name: Coverage exclusions
derived_requirements.description: What is knowingly excluded from this element's population, and whether the materiality of that exclusion has been assessed, per ¶43.

standards.purpose: Establish, for each critical data element, whether an availability SLA is defined and whether the capability has been tested under stress conditions. Principle 5 sets different speed expectations per risk type, and requires the capability to hold when it matters most.
standards.scope: Every critical data element on the critical path of a reported risk figure.

derived_requirements.name: Availability SLA
derived_requirements.description: Whether a timeliness target is defined for this element, per ¶44-45.

derived_requirements.name: Stress-condition capability
derived_requirements.description: Whether the ability to deliver this element within its SLA has been tested under stress, per ¶46-47.

standard_attachment.$comment: Which standards attach to a CDE is DERIVABLE from the principles in its driven_by, not inferred. Neither agent needs to know policies exist.
